Ava —

Thanks again for the time today. As we discussed, before we lock the MAP and finalize the pilot purchase order we need to validate a few unit-economics assumptions so procurement can sign off. I attached the traffic profile you shared and a draft MAP (MSH_MAP_v1.docx) with proposed milestones. Can you confirm the following from your side?

- Peak QPS and steady-state QPS (hourly) for the pilot (you mentioned ~120 qps peak earlier)
- Typical prompt length and expected tokens per API call (input + response) for the clinical summarization endpoint
- Whether patient-level session affinity is required (affects KV cache hit rates)
- Expected concurrency per operator (agents running summaries in parallel)

On our side we want to run a focused unit-econ check (tokens/$, batching, and caching assumptions) and return a short numeric summary that you can give to procurement. Suggested timeline: econ check + small batching sim by EOD 6/2, MAP update with final numbers 6/3, PO/Procurement signature target 6/9. Is that cadence doable?

Attachments: MSH_traffic_profile.xlsx, MSH_MAP_v1.docx

Thanks — I’ll loop in engineering and solutions to validate batching and caching tradeoffs.

—Karthik

Karthik —

Thanks, that all looks right. Quick answers inline:

- Peak QPS: 120 peak (burst to 180 for 10–15 min during morning shift). Steady-state: 45 qps.
- Tokens: average prompt ~320 tokens (clinical note + instructions), expected model response ~220 tokens so ~540 tokens per call.
- Session affinity: we do not require strict session affinity across requests; we can accept per-request routing to improve cache hit rates, but retaining the same patient context in the app is preferred.
- Concurrency: each operator typically runs 2–3 parallel tasks during peak.

Two follow-ups: first, what batching assumptions do you intend to validate? We want to ensure latency SLOs remain under 800ms p95. Second, will you include a KV cache hit-rate sensitivity (we expect ~60% hit rate with per-request routing)?

If you can send a short econ table we can circulate to procurement today.

Best,
Ava Mitchell
Head of Clinical Ops, MediScale Health

Team —

Forwarding Ava's reply. She confirmed traffic and gave an expected ~540 tokens/call and a ~60% KV cache hit-rate target if we do per-request routing. Procurement wants a short table they can use to greenlight the PO. Primarily we need: tokens-per-dollar at 3 candidate configs and latency implications. Priorities:

1) Baseline: no quantization, batching disabled (per-request), KV cache 60%
2) Efficiency: 8-bit quant variant, batching factor 4, KV cache 60%
3) Aggressive: 4-bit/quantized variant, batching factor 8, KV cache 75% (assuming we recommend prefetching patient context)

Constraints: keep p95 latency <= 800ms for Baseline and Efficiency; Aggressive can degrade to 1.2s p95 if we note it in MAP. Please run a quick sim and give a tokens/$ and estimated p95 for each config. Attach any worksheets to the thread. Target: initial econ table by EOD 6/2 so I can carve into the MAP and send to Ava.

Thanks — Karthik
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-06-02T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP: unit economics & cost validation for close

Karthik / Neha —

Attached is a compact econ workbook (karthik_msh_econ_v3.xlsx) and raw sim results (batching_sim_results.csv). High-level summary below (assumptions: 540 tokens/call, 120 qps peak, average session tokens 540, model baseline per-token cost $0.0000105 for the unquantized variant):

Summary table (tokens per USD, est p95 latency):
- Baseline (no quant, no batch, KV hit 60%): ~95k tokens/$; est p95 620ms (meets 800ms SLA)
- Efficiency (8-bit quant, batch x4, KV hit 60%): ~320k tokens/$; est p95 740ms (still under 800ms)
- Aggressive (4-bit quant, batch x8, KV hit 75%): ~1.1M tokens/$; est p95 1.15s (exceeds 800ms — note in MAP)

Key notes and sensitivity:
- KV cache: moving from 60% -> 75% reduces RPU (requests processed by the model) by ~33%, which compounds with batching to significantly improve tokens/$. Recommend prefetching patient context for top 20% of flows to move toward 70% hit-rate.
- Batching: we simulated micro-batching with Redwood runtime; batching factor of 4 gives diminishing returns after 6 for this workload due to request variance. Latency impact is linear with batch size under our sim distribution; we included p95 numbers.
- Quantization: 8-bit yields modest latency improvement and big cost upside; 4-bit gives large token/$ but comes with quality risk — call out in MAP as optional canary.

Attachments included: karthik_msh_econ_v3.xlsx (summary pivot + assumptions), batching_sim_results.csv (per-run latencies).

Let me know if you want me to tighten the p95 sims with a stricter latency budget or generate a one-page econ table for procurement.

—Priyom
